CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR  ORAL ORDER

This petition is by the accused Nos. 1 and 2 in S.C. No.1033/2018 on the file of the LIII Additional City Civil and Sessions Special Judge, Bengaluru challenging the order dated 01st July, 2023,
whereby, the application filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to recall the complainant who was examined as PW1 to cross-examine her was rejected.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the respondents and perused the material on record.

3. A perusal of the material on record will indicate that the respondent No.2-complainant had instituted the aforesaid proceedings against the petitioners for the alleged offence punishable under Sections 420, 376, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC
In the said proceedings, the respondent No.2-complainant examined herself as PW1 and was cross-examined by the petitioners.

Subsequently, the petitioners-accused Nos. 1 and 2 having filed the application under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to recall the PW1 for further cross- examination, the learned Magistrate rejected the said application by passing the impugned order, which is assailed in the present petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, if the impugned order is set-aside and the petitioners-accused Nos. 1 and 2 are permitted to cross-examine the PW1 further, the petitioners would complete the cross-examination of the PW1 on the next date of hearing before the Trial Court without NC: 2025:KHC:24808 HC-KAR seeking any adjournment under any circumstances whatsoever.

It is therefore submitted that the impugned order be set-aside and application filed by the petitioners under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to recall the PW1 for further cross- examine be allowed.
5.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents opposed the petition and submits that there is no merit in the petition and same is liable to be dismissed.

6. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, though several contentions have been urged by learned counsel for both sides, by adopting a justice oriented approach and in order to provide one more opportunity to the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2, I deem it appropriate to allow the petition by imposing exemplary cost upon the petitioners with certain terms and conditions upon the petitioners with a direction to the Trial Court to dispose of the proceedings within a stipulated time frame.
